_comment: Hand-written raw-spec.json, used by checks.resolve-lazy-self's version step (#49): a
git-type lazy.nvim fork with a `version` constraint, exercising the semver gate for the
`url` here is a placeholder -- the check overwrites .plugins["lazy.nvim"].url with `jq`
before every use, pointing it at a local git repo it creates itself (mkTagRepoSh), so the
constraint can be resolved with no network at all. This has to be git type, not github: a
github-type version constraint does `git ls-remote` against the literal `p.url` in resolve.lua's
semver-resolution ls-remote loop, which cannot be redirected to a local repo -- see
docs/plans/29-genflake-golden.md's own note on the same constraint.
This fixture's `lazy.nvim` key is itself a hand-written-only shape: extracting a real
`{ url = "file:///.../lazy" }` spec entry would derive the plugin name from the URL's
basename ("lazy"), never "lazy.nvim" -- lazy only derives "lazy.nvim" from a URL whose last
path segment literally ends in "lazy.nvim" (e.g. a GitHub fork URL, see the plan's §1.5). A
hand-written fixture can set the raw.plugins key directly, bypassing that derivation, which is
